title: The Method
subtitle: Four frameworks, used in the same order every time. Each has its own page. This one shows how they fit together.

sections.heading: Four Frameworks, One Path
sections.body:
Every engagement uses the same four frameworks, in the same order: qualify, diagnose, execute, learn. The first two are the core of a Readiness Assessment. The last two carry the work that follows.

Each framework answers one question. If you only read one page, read the one whose question is yours.

sections.heading: 1. Qualify: 6Sense Filter
sections.body:
The question: should we work together at all?

Six-dimensional qualification gate. Screens for genuine market demand, a sustainable business model, operational capability, strategic focus, regulatory risk, and decision-making quality. A longer partnership requires all six.

> The 6Sense Filter opens every engagement, as part of the Readiness Assessment. If your company does not pass all six dimensions, I say so, early and clearly. The filter exists to protect both parties.

[Read about the 6Sense Filter](/6sense.html)

sections.heading: 2. Diagnose: AI Compass
sections.body:
The question: where does the company stand today?

1-to-5 star diagnostic of AI governance maturity. Maps where a company actually is, from no inventory of its AI systems and no named owner (1 star) to independently assured governance (5 stars). Prescribes a sequenced path forward.

[Read about AI Compass](/ai-compass.html)

sections.heading: 3. Execute: Polaris Sprints
sections.body:
The question: what must be true in 90 days?

Execution architecture and performance governance. Tracks the metrics that drive capital decisions — customer profitability, delivery performance, cash flow efficiency, and operational capacity. Ensures digital product sprints and regulatory compliance milestones move in lockstep.

[Read about Polaris Sprints](/polaris.html)

sections.heading: 4. Learn: Kando Framework
sections.body:
The question: what did we learn from what went wrong?

Operational execution and crisis intelligence. Applies Theory of Constraints and Drum-Buffer-Rope logic to executive capacity management. Converts negative events (lost deals, churn, complaints, audit findings) into structured strategic intelligence.

[Read about the Kando Framework](/kando.html)

sections.heading: See It Applied
sections.body:
The clearest way into the method is to watch it used. Method in Practice follows two fictitious companies through the steps, with the numbers: one that sells to the established players, and one that competes with them.

[See the method applied to an example company](/example.html)

sections.heading: What Is Tested and What Is Not
sections.body: The frameworks were developed in practice and then grounded in established management theory. They have not yet been independently validated; the [Research](/research.html) page sets out what that would take.
